significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that query language predictively couples to culturally conditioned answer distributions and that a compact residual-stream "cultural context" direction causally controls this coupling; this combines a form-(iii) predictive relation with a form-(ii) mechanism. It would establish both a phenomenon—defaults "systematic and predictable from the cultural region associated with each language"—and a mechanism "largely separate from factual-knowledge subspaces," fixing expectations across multiple underspecified domains and linking behavioral variation to latent-language organization studied in work such as GlobalOpinionQA (Durmus et al., 2023) and Wendler et al. (ACL 2024). A clean behavioral null would support a monocultural or language-invariant default, but falsity of the bundled mechanism could instead mean that the representation is distributed or entangled, so true and false are distinguishable while the negative mechanistic branch is not uniquely diagnostic. In the topic-substitution check, generic questions about shared versus language-specific representations would not justify this score; the specific cultural-distance coupling and causal decoupling claim are what raise it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Cultural-Default-Alignment score" and, more importantly, the steerable "cultural context" direction that lets answers be "grounded in a chosen alternative cultural context." Steering is ex ante because it changes the contextual default before an answer is generated, giving model-localization or deployment practitioners an action window rather than only explaining an observed failure. The intervention direction would require re-extraction on each model and does not predict its new coordinates, although the asserted relation between language-associated cultural region and default distributions should survive recalibration across languages, models, and classes of underspecified questions. In the topic-substitution check, the broad multilingual-representation topic alone supplies neither this intervention nor practitioner uptake; those claim-specific features support reach above the median, though not the highest band because transfer of the causal direction itself is not asserted as invariant.
